title: The Animals We Sent to War
description:
Dogs have officially served in the US military since 1942, and they are one of the least surprising animals ever sent to war. The CIA wired a cat with a microphone and a transmitter. Armed bats set part of an American airfield on fire. Pigeons were trained to steer a missile. A messenger pigeon called Cher Ami became a legend. Polish soldiers adopted a bear, and the Marines made a horse a staff sergeant. This episode also covers the Soviet anti-tank dogs, the horses of the First World War, a Newfoundland dog named Gander, and the dolphins and rats that are still working today. Some of these stories sound almost fun. But the animals weren't volunteers.

Chapters
00:00 Dogs join the army
00:59 The first animals in space
02:30 The really bad ideas
06:00 The ones that actually worked
09:30 They had no choice
11:26 We're still doing it
13:17 What do you think?

title: Could AI End the World?
description:
In September 2026, AI researcher Jacob Coxon quit his job at Anthropic and warned that AI could kill us all by the end of the decade. So could it actually happen? This episode looks at the three ways AI could go wrong, losing control, misuse and slow damage, and then at what we could gain if it goes right.

01:09 The warning signs

09:03 3. Slow damage
